About Lumina'26 Hackathon

Fuel your logic, spark your genius — it's time to build without limits!

Under the banner of LUMINA, IEEE Student Branch JIIT presents Lumina'26 Hackathon, a 24-hour innovation marathon where ideas turn into technology-driven solutions.

For 24 hours, participants will brainstorm, design, develop, test, and build solutions to real-world problems. Whether you're a developer, designer, researcher, problem-solver, or someone with an unconventional idea, Lumina is a space to experiment, collaborate, and create.

Bring your boldest ideas, sharpest skills, and curiosity to question the ordinary.

Join the whatsapp group : https://chat.whatsapp.com/COiVas6p82zKrPzpLXQ3sT?s=cl&p=a&mlu=4&ilr=4&iam=0

Theme: Hack the Unseen

 

Build solutions for the problems that hide in plain sight — the everyday frustrations, overlooked inefficiencies, and challenges that people have simply learned to live with.

 

Look beyond the obvious and rethink the ordinary. Your mission is to discover an overlooked problem and turn an unconventional idea into a practical, technology-enabled solution that creates a real impact.

 

Example directions (but not limited to):

 

- Hidden inefficiencies in everyday routines and systems

- Accessibility challenges that often go unnoticed

- Tools for underserved or overlooked communities

- Digital safety, fraud detection, privacy, and online threats

- Making essential services more accessible and efficient

- Public infrastructure and civic-tech solutions

- Small everyday problems that technology could solve better

- Sustainability and waste problems hidden in ordinary activities

 

The problem doesn't have to be huge — it just has to be unseen.

 

If you can discover a problem others overlook and build a solution that makes people ask, "Why didn't we have this before?", it fits the theme.

Eligibility & Participation Guidelines

  • Each team must have 3–4 members. Each team should have at least one female member.
  • Teams can have members from different years or branches.
  • Each participant can be part of only one team.
  • Teams must use original ideas and code (no plagiarism).

Hackathon Format

  • Duration: 24 hours of non-stop innovation
  • Date: Starts at 12 PM on 28th October 2026
  • Venue: Online (Virtual Mode)
  • Team Size: 3–4 members (must include atleast 1 female participant)

Participants will go through the following stages:

1. Commencement of the Hack (28th October 2026 : 12PM)
Teams begin ideation, development, testing, and implementation of their solutions.

2. Mid Evaluation (28th October 2026 : 8PM)
Teams submit a brief overview of their problem statement, proposed solution, and progress. They may be required to present their progress to the evaluation panel.

3. Final Submission (29th October 2026 : 12PM)
Teams submit their final presentation, project/demo video, and working prototype or project link, wherever applicable.

4. Final Evaluation (29th October 2026 : 8PM)
Shortlisted teams present their solutions to the judges. Projects will be evaluated based on the quality of the problem identified, innovation, technical implementation, impact, feasibility, and overall presentation.

Expected Deliverables

Teams may be required to submit:

  • Proposed solution
  • Presentation/PPT
  • Working prototype or project
  • Demo/video submission
  • Project repository or deployment link, wherever applicable

Specific submission instructions and deadlines will be communicated to registered participants.

Evaluation Criteria

Judges will evaluate based on:

  • Innovation & Creativity – How unique and original is the idea?
  • Impact & Relevance – Does it genuinely help the community?
  • Technical Implementation – Functionality, scalability, and quality of the prototype.
  • Design & User Experience – How intuitive and user-friendly is the solution?
  • Presentation – Clarity and effectiveness of the demo and explanation.

General Rules

  • The solution should be developed in accordance with the hackathon theme.
  • Teams must consist of 3–4 members.
  • Participants are expected to build their solutions during the hackathon period, subject to the event's specific rules.
  • Teams may use publicly available APIs, libraries, frameworks, datasets, and other permitted resources.
  • Any third-party resources used should be properly acknowledged.
  • Plagiarism or submission of substantially pre-built projects may lead to disqualification.
  • Each team should submit only one final project.
  • Decisions of the organizing and judging panel will be final.

What’s in it for You

  • Certificates for all participants.
  • Exciting prizes for top teams.
  • Opportunity to get your solution featured under WIE’s tech initiatives.
  • 24 hours of learning, teamwork, and innovation!

What Are You Waiting For?

Think differently. Question the ordinary. Find what others overlook.

Hack the Unseen.

Build what the world didn't know it needed.
